verdict: No unresolved findings. Two scalar-storage contract differences found during review were fixed and independently verified.
scope: Independent big review of bounded exact transcendental caches, signed power-of-two division replacements, certified 112-bit candidate enclosures, and static scalar-stack promotion. This report does not claim universal native-vendor transcendental equivalence, raster identity, or a browser FPS measurement. Shared Float80 and compact frame arithmetic received a separate review; the corresponding files are pinned here as dependencies.
cleared: Generated drawing outputs are reviewed through exact regeneration of all 251 baseline functions and the generator eligibility proof rather than individual formatting comments.

resolvedFindings.issue: An I32 store whose nonsemantic host-like object has a false pointer field must retain the original DataView ToNumber coercion.
resolvedFindings.trigger: {frame:null}, {array:null}, {dc:null}, or similar objects with a valueOf implementation.
resolvedFindings.originalEvidence: Independently imported HEAD typed-c.js and compared original storage against compact and scalar storage: original returned 0 for all three plain objects while both optimized stores returned the object.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The semantic guard still preserves real semantic identities. Scalar I32 storage now applies (+cI32(value))|0, and compact-frame storage received the corresponding fix. Regression inputs include positive/negative custom valueOf conversions and thrown/BigInt/Symbol conversion results.

resolvedFindings.issue: A finite extended value may overflow at a binary64 store and be overwritten before a later load; early scalar-store rejection changed observable behavior.
resolvedFindings.trigger: new Float80(1,1n<<63n,2000), store to F64, overwrite with 7, then read. Original byte storage returned 7; the initial scalar helper threw at the first store.
resolvedFindings.resolution: A private stored-nonfinite marker defers the original floating load failure until scalarRead or scalarReadArgument. Undefined argument propagation and invalid Number Infinity/NaN store failures retain their original timing. The generator now routes F64 argument reads through scalarReadArgument.

checkedClean: Both caches retain at most 2,048 entries, distinguish full canonical m80 values and signed zero, include the x87 control word, and cache only successful evaluations.
Cached Float80 components remain immutable. Sin/cos returns a fresh mutable pair; zero and sufficiently tiny input identity shortcuts run without cache retention.
Magnitude right shifts followed by sign restoration exactly preserve BigInt truncation toward zero for the old divisions by 2^224.
The 224-bit Machin PI and 66-bit x87 quadrant reduction are unchanged. Mathematical sin/cos retains the complete 224-bit series.

The candidate is accepted only after its domain and termination guards and only when the entire conservative integer enclosure rounds to one canonical m80 value. Ambiguous or near-zero enclosures keep the original 224-bit path.

The static local pass requires literal in-frame I32/F64 offsets, one view per slot, disjoint slots, no escaping localFrame identifier, and complete discarded-result write statements. Nested reads are preserved in evaluation order.
Explicit retained-byte inputs, including empty arrays, use the unchanged byte frame. The retained options property is observed once; malformed initialization and missing-byte failures remain visible.

analyticalEnclosure.scales: S=2^112; original scale T=2^224; K=T/S=2^112. Both algorithms use signed truncation toward zero. The certified interval is [candidate-1024,candidate+1024] in S units.

sinCos.domain: After the unchanged 224-bit x87 reduction, the reduced candidate has |a/S|<1.
sinCos.termBound: Truncating the squared argument changes it by <1 scale unit. Each product introduces <1 further unit before division by d. With |term/scale|<=1 and d>=2, term error obeys E_next < E_previous/2+2, hence E<4 units.
sinCos.terminationAndTail: Magnitude truncation cannot enlarge a Taylor term; scale/(2n)! is below 1 for n=64 at either precision. The first omitted alternating term has magnitude <4 units. At most 64 per-term errors plus the tail give <260 units at each algorithm scale.
sinCos.candidateToOriginal: Input quantization changes sin/cos by <1 fast unit. The combined candidate-to-original error is <261+260/K <262 fast units; quadrant sign/permutation does not enlarge it. This is below 1024.

atan.domain: The direct or transformed series has |a/scale|<=1/2; the ratio transform preserves this domain. Threshold quantization may choose a different branch, but both branches approximate the same atan of the exact ratio.
atan.termBound: Squared-input truncation and power truncation obey E_next < E_previous/4+1.5, so E<2 units. Divided-term errors are <2 units.
atan.terminationAndTail: Successive powers contract by at least 1/4, so both precisions terminate within 113 iterations. A conservative sum-and-tail bound is <229 units at the respective scale.
atan.piAndTransforms: The untouched Machin PI error is below 20*(229+1)=4600 original units. Ratio quantization, the transform and its rounding, FAST_PI truncation, and integer PI divisions/quadrants fit inside the stated additional bounds. Quadrant coefficients of PI have magnitude at most 1.
atan.candidateToOriginal: A conservative bound is <240 fast units +10000 original units, i.e. <241 fast units. This covers the original integer series as well as the mathematical function and is below 1024.

analyticalEnclosure.rounding: Float80 construction always performs canonical 64-bit nearest/even normalization. That rounding is monotone for finite values. Identical sign, mantissa and exponent at both enclosure endpoints therefore establish the same result for the enclosed original 224-bit integer. A crossing of zero or a rounding boundary rejects the candidate.

independentIntegerChecks.scope: Independent unrounded integer comparison: both 112-bit and original 224-bit recurrence evaluated with direct BigInt division, including quantization, ratio transform, unchanged PI and all atan quadrants. This verifies sampled enclosure membership, not a replacement for the analytical bound or a native-vendor claim.

checks.check: Independently invoke promote_static_locals on each HEAD routine, compare every emitted fast/fallback function and eligibility record to the final generated sources.
